GW5 · Completed

GW5 · THE McDRAFT COLUMN

Backstreet Moyes did not so much beat Jaap? Best Stam as redecorate the room with them, running out 58-31 winners. The Bald Derby supplied its usual dignity and restraint, with Backstreet Moyes beating Jaap? Best Stam 58-31 to own the bragging rights for now. PAUer Rangers spent GW5 climbing over furniture and rivals alike, moving from 4th to 3rd. Kamararama FC's horseshoe remains securely installed, with the Luck Index now reading +5.1. The hottest streak in town belongs to Kamararama FC, now winners of 5 in a row. Individual dishonour goes to J.Timber, whose 0-point contribution did precisely nothing for No Weimann No Cry's blood pressure. Somewhere a single bonus point is feeling extremely important: Jacquet Potato squeezed past danny’s doggy dudes 37-36. There are points lying on the pavement. Vuskovic, Janelt and Egan are still free agents and increasingly difficult to explain away. GW6 offers Jaap? Best Stam against PAUer Rangers — currently 4th versus 3rd; one of those matches that could look very important indeed by Monday night.

Rest-of-Season Prediction

A schedule-aware Monte Carlo forecast of the remaining season. Model estimate, not destiny — one monster haul can still make a right bloody mess of it.

Model: 7,500 Monte Carlo simulations using the real remaining H2H schedule. Current squad strength and recent form still drive the forecast, but early-season weekly expectations are deliberately regressed hard towards the league mean and score volatility is widened. Finishing probabilities are then calibrated back towards the league baseline until enough gameweeks have been played, so five good weeks cannot create fake certainty. The calibration now fades through roughly the first 10 completed GWs, so stronger teams separate earlier while early-season confidence remains restrained. Squad strength still uses the best legal projected XI, recent/season output and original McDraft rank as a decaying prior. Confidence badges describe how much evidence the forecast currently has; they are not another prediction. Forecast Range is the central 80% of simulated finishes and remains separate from mathematical Possible Finish.

THE STORY OF GW1

GW1 saw Backstreet Moyes lead the way, banking 59 points.

No Weimann No Cry had a week to forget after NoRSNoRB No Chance blew them away 53-29.

danny’s doggy dudes brought up the rear with 24 points and will probably be happy to see the back of GW1. At the other end of the drama scale, Kamararama FC scraped past PAUer Rangers 29-26.

Season Diary

Newest first. Each chunky weekly column is built from results, table movement, rivalries, trades, player performances, luck and the following week's fixtures.

GW5

Backstreet Moyes did not so much beat Jaap? Best Stam as redecorate the room with them, running out 58-31 winners. The Bald Derby supplied its usual dignity and restraint, with Backstreet Moyes beating Jaap? Best Stam 58-31 to own the bragging rights for now. PAUer Rangers spent GW5 climbing over furniture and rivals alike, moving from 4th to 3rd. Kamararama FC's horseshoe remains securely installed, with the Luck Index now reading +5.1. The hottest streak in town belongs to Kamararama FC, now winners of 5 in a row. Individual dishonour goes to J.Timber, whose 0-point contribution did precisely nothing for No Weimann No Cry's blood pressure. Somewhere a single bonus point is feeling extremely important: Jacquet Potato squeezed past danny’s doggy dudes 37-36. There are points lying on the pavement. Vuskovic, Janelt and Egan are still free agents and increasingly difficult to explain away. GW6 offers Jaap? Best Stam against PAUer Rangers — currently 4th versus 3rd; one of those matches that could look very important indeed by Monday night.

GW4

Move over, previous leader. Kamararama FC took control of McDraft in GW4, climbing to first after another weekend of entirely normal fantasy behaviour. Nobody climbed faster than PAUer Rangers, up from 6th to 4th and suddenly looking much taller. The trapdoor opened beneath NoRSNoRB No Chance, who fell from 5th to 7th. Fortune currently has Kamararama FC on speed dial. Their Luck Index is +4.4, which is beginning to look less like a bounce and more like a sponsorship deal. If anybody fancies doing some actual recruitment, Belloumi, Egan and Giles remain available and are making increasingly persuasive little noises in the scoring charts. A cough in the wrong direction could have changed danny’s doggy dudes v NoRSNoRB No Chance; instead danny’s doggy dudes held on 45-44. Kamararama FC have won 4 consecutive games and may soon need to be reminded that humility is technically available. Awoniyi produced -2 for Kamararama FC, bringing all the explosive force of a damp party popper. Next week's main event is unmistakable — The Bald Derby, Backstreet Moyes against Jaap? Best Stam, with Backstreet Moyes sitting 2nd and Jaap? Best Stam 3rd. The points matter; the bragging rights matter far more.

GW3

The mercy rule does not exist in McDraft, which was unfortunate for PAUer Rangers: Backstreet Moyes vaporised them 67-39. Kamararama FC found the express lane, leaping 2 places to 2nd. Somebody greased the ladder under danny’s doggy dudes: 8th became 10th by Monday. A special mention for Thiaw: -1 points for Jaap? Best Stam and several minutes of staring blankly at the app. The fantasy gods have apparently added Kamararama FC to close friends; a +4.4 Luck Index tells its own suspicious little story. Make it 3 on the spin for Backstreet Moyes; whatever switch they flicked, somebody should probably unplug it. Backstreet Moyes got a serious lift from Mitchell, whose 15-point haul was the individual performance of the round. A cough in the wrong direction could have changed Kamararama FC v Jaap? Best Stam; instead Kamararama FC held on 40-38. Eyes forward: Backstreet Moyes and Kamararama FC collide in GW4 — currently 1st versus 2nd, a fixture with enough table consequence to make everyone pretend they are not checking live points every four minutes.

GW2

The week's loudest thud came from Backstreet Moyes, who dropped a 59-24 piano on Buendophilia. danny’s doggy dudes found the express lane, leaping 2 places to 8th. It was a less glamorous weekend for NoRSNoRB No Chance, sliding from 2nd to 5th and discovering gravity is undefeated. Top billing among the players goes to B.Fernandes, a 23-point menace in Ollie Gonna Squashya's colours. The fixture computer owes Jacquet Potato an apology card. A -3.0 Luck Index and 58.5 points against on average is grim reading. Individual dishonour goes to Vuskovic, whose 0-point contribution did precisely nothing for Jaap? Best Stam's blood pressure. Somebody found the trade button: No Weimann No Cry moved Eze, Awoniyi to Kamararama FC for Rayan, Strand Larsen. That one has all the ingredients to be revisited later in the season. Scouting departments may want to put the kettle down: Egan, Lewis-Potter and Groß remain unattached despite elbowing their way up the scoring lists. The circus rolls into GW3 with Kamararama FC v Jaap? Best Stam — currently 4th versus 2nd looking especially tasty.

GW1

GW1's crime scene was NoRSNoRB No Chance 53, No Weimann No Cry 29. Detectives have described the margin as 'unnecessary'. There was no room for oxygen between Kamararama FC and PAUer Rangers: 29-26 to Kamararama FC, by the skin of several teeth. If NoRSNoRB No Chance are writing thank-you cards, Palmer gets the first one after a monster 13-point haul. A special mention for Colwill: 0 points for No Weimann No Cry and several minutes of staring blankly at the app. Variance has put Jacquet Potato in a headlock: -2.3 on the Luck Index and an opponent average of 59.0. Recruitment departments, wake up: De Cuyper, Kayode and Stach are still unattached and are making the free-agent pool look far less barren than it has any right to be. Eyes forward: Ollie Gonna Squashya and NoRSNoRB No Chance collide in GW2 — currently 4th versus 2nd, a fixture with enough table consequence to make everyone pretend they are not checking live points every four minutes.
